LESSON: SELF- ESTEEM ASSESSMENT

Grade: Grade 8
Subject: SOCIAL STUDIES
Strand: Social Studies Personal Management
Topic 1.2: Self- Esteem Assessment

SECTION 1: WELCOME

Hello! This is a study lesson on Self- Esteem Assessment. Read the explanation, follow every worked example, then do the practice. This is original CBC Learn content written from KICD outcomes — not a copy of a commercial textbook.

Big question: How does self- esteem affect my holistic development?

SECTION 2: WHAT YOU WILL LEARN

By the end of this lesson, you will be able to:

1. explain the contribution of self- esteem on their holistic development
2. identify a problem/gap in the community
3. appreciate the need to offer solutions to the gaps/challenges in the community

SECTION 3: STUDY NOTES (READ AND LEARN)

WHAT YOU ARE STUDYING: SELF- ESTEEM ASSESSMENT
Subject: SOCIAL STUDIES · Grade: Grade 8
This is a learner study lesson (not a teacher guide). Read every part, follow the models, then practise.

BIG PICTURE
Self- Esteem Assessment helps you succeed in SOCIAL STUDIES. You will understand it, practise it, and use it in your county, school, and Kenyan community.

KEY FACTS: SELF- ESTEEM ASSESSMENT
Good citizens follow rules, respect others, and care for shared places.
Kenyan examples: lining up, keeping the compound clean, telling the truth, helping a classmate.
Rights come with responsibilities.

PART 1: Explain the contribution of self- esteem on their holistic development

What this means
In this part you learn to explain the contribution of self- esteem on their holistic development. You will use ideas from in your county, school, and Kenyan community.

How to learn it
1. Read the idea carefully: explain the contribution of self- esteem on their holistic development.
2. Locate, explain, then act responsibly using a Kenyan example from your life.
3. Check yourself: Can you explain it without looking?

Model
Locate: Connect “Self- Esteem Assessment” to a real place or group in Kenya (school, market, county office, home).

Your turn
Do one short practice that proves you can explain the contribution of self- esteem on their holistic development. Write or say your answer clearly.

PART 2: Identify a problem/gap in the community

What this means
In this part you learn to identify a problem/gap in the community. You will use ideas from in your county, school, and Kenyan community.

How to learn it
1. Read the idea carefully: identify a problem/gap in the community.
2. Locate, explain, then act responsibly using a Kenyan example from your life.
3. Check yourself: Can you explain it without looking?

Model
Explain: Give one cause and one effect linked to Self- Esteem Assessment.

Your turn
Do one short practice that proves you can identify a problem/gap in the community. Write or say your answer clearly.

PART 3: Appreciate the need to offer solutions to the gaps/challenges in the community

What this means
In this part you learn to appreciate the need to offer solutions to the gaps/challenges in the community. You will use ideas from in your county, school, and Kenyan community.

How to learn it
1. Read the idea carefully: appreciate the need to offer solutions to the gaps/challenges in the community.
2. Locate, explain, then act responsibly using a Kenyan example from your life.
3. Check yourself: Can you explain it without looking?

Model
Participate: Describe one responsible action a Grade learner can take.

Your turn
Do one short practice that proves you can appreciate the need to offer solutions to the gaps/challenges in the community. Write or say your answer clearly.

PUT IT TOGETHER
Close your notes and say aloud: what Self- Esteem Assessment is, one example, and one way you will practise this week.

SECTION 4: QUICK EXAMPLES

Good citizens follow rules, respect others, and care for shared places.

Kenyan examples: lining up, keeping the compound clean, telling the truth, helping a classmate.

Example 1: Connect “Self- Esteem Assessment” to a real place or group in Kenya (school, market, county office, home). (skill: explain the contribution of self- esteem on their holistic development)

Example 2: Give one cause and one effect linked to Self- Esteem Assessment. (skill: identify a problem/gap in the community)

Example 3: Describe one responsible action a Grade learner can take. (skill: appreciate the need to offer solutions to the gaps/challenges in the community)

SECTION 5: PRACTICE NOW

1. Write 5 sentences (or show 5 clear steps) that teach Self- Esteem Assessment to a classmate.
2. Practise this skill: explain the contribution of self- esteem on their holistic development.
3. Practise this skill: identify a problem/gap in the community.
4. Practise this skill: appreciate the need to offer solutions to the gaps/challenges in the community.
5. Make one local Kenya example of Self- Esteem Assessment from your county, market, farm, or school.
6. Mark your own work: What did you get right? What will you redo?

SECTION 6: WORK TO DO (HOME / REVISION)

1. In your exercise book, make a one-page revision sheet for Self- Esteem Assessment: meaning, 3 examples, 5 practice items.
2. Teach a parent/guardian or younger sibling one part of this lesson (2 minutes).
3. Answer in writing: Why should a Grade 8 learner study Self- Esteem Assessment?
4. Prepare for the quiz: cover the Remember box and recite it.

SECTION: THINK ABOUT IT

1. How does self- esteem affect my holistic development?
2. How does one determine some gaps/ needs in the community?
3. Why is it necessary to make adequate preparations before embarking on a project?

SECTION: REMEMBER

1. Know what Self- Esteem Assessment means in your own words.
2. Use local Kenyan examples, not only definitions.
3. Practise in small steps, then check your work.
4. Be able to: explain the contribution of self- esteem on their holistic development.
5. Be able to: identify a problem/gap in the community.

Now complete the Revision Quiz. Open Answers only after you finish.

— CBC Learn · Original study notes from KICD outcomes (Strategy 2)
